facts.text: Blockton was founded in 1861 by a dozen Cutlerite Mormon families led by Alpheus Cutler, who moved from Manti in Fremont County.
The town was originally called Mormontown; a post office opened in 1872, and the name changed to Blockton in 1887 after the Mormons departed.
Blockton was officially incorporated as a city on March 28, 1890, following its renaming and growth as the largest village in Jefferson Township.
Two mills built by the Mormon pioneers powered early local industry, but the mills vanished after the settlers returned to Manti by 1865.
The Blockton News, founded in 1887, chronicled the town’s expansion and railway influence until its final issue in 1944.
Blockton lies just east of the Platte River, with the Ringgold–Taylor county line marking its eastern boundary.
